content.user_title: Qualify Prospects Against Your GTM Criteria
content.value_statement: Manual fit checks produce inconsistent decisions across people and companies. This skill applies saved personas and ICPs to deliver structured, evidence-based qualification.
actual_capabilities: Qualifies people against visible saved personas.
Qualifies companies against visible saved ICPs.
Separates person and company scoring into distinct modes.
Assigns fit bands, numeric scores, confidence levels, and evidence-based reasoning.
Handles single prospects, pasted rows, profile URLs, domains, and local CSV paths.
Requests exact-scope approval before paid identity or enrichment calls.
limitations: Requires a connected GTM workspace with relevant visible personas or ICPs.
Evaluates fit only and does not score intent, engagement, or purchase timing.
Does not create, edit, or repair workspace artifacts.
Does not persist results or support scheduled high-volume scoring.

use_cases.title: Prioritize target accounts
use_cases.description: Compare supplied companies with saved ICPs and rank them by fit band and confidence.

use_cases.title: Review inbound leads
use_cases.description: Match individual prospects to saved personas and identify strong, weak, or uncertain fits.

use_cases.title: Calibrate qualification criteria
use_cases.description: Test known positive and negative examples to identify unclear persona or ICP criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Qualify one company
prompt_templates.prompt: Qualify Acme Corporation against our saved ICPs. Explain the fit, score, confidence, and matched ICP.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a quick account fit check.

prompt_templates.title: Qualify one person
prompt_templates.prompt: Qualify Jordan Lee at Acme Corporation against our saved personas using available public information.
prompt_templates.scenario: A representative needs to assess one contact.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a prospect list
prompt_templates.prompt: Qualify these prospects. Separate people from companies, match each to the best artifact, and sort results by band and confidence: [paste rows].
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a structured review of mixed prospect rows.

prompt_templates.title: Calibrate saved criteria
prompt_templates.prompt: Qualify these known strong and weak examples against our saved artifacts. Identify repeated scoring mismatches without editing any artifact: [paste examples].
prompt_templates.scenario: Revenue operations is testing qualification consistency.

output_examples.input: Qualify Acme Corporation against our saved ICPs.
output_examples.output:
Verdict: Good
Score: 78
Confidence: Medium
Scored against: Mid-Market SaaS
Reasoning: Acme matches the target industry and size. Geography remains unverified. Band: Good.

output_examples.input: Qualify Jordan Lee at Acme Corporation against our personas.
output_examples.output:
Verdict: Insufficient data
Scored against: Revenue Leader
Reasoning: Multiple people share this name and employer. Identity remains unresolved after available free research.

best_practices: Provide clear names, domains, employers, or public profile URLs to reduce identity ambiguity.
Keep persona and ICP criteria specific enough to support evidence-based decisions.
Review confidence and unknown fields before acting on a numeric score.
anti_patterns: Do not use fit scores as measures of intent, engagement, or purchase timing.
Do not combine person attributes with company attributes in one score.
Do not use this skill for recurring or scheduled bulk qualification.

faq.question: What can this skill qualify?
faq.answer: It qualifies supplied people against saved personas and supplied companies against saved ICPs.

faq.question: Does it require a GTM workspace?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs a connected workspace with visible personas or ICPs for the requested mode.

faq.question: Can it process several prospects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can process pasted rows or a local CSV path and returns separate person and company tables.

faq.question: Does it use paid enrichment?
faq.answer: Only after an exact-scope approval that states the entities, provider capability, call count, effect, and available cost information.

faq.question: What happens when data is missing?
faq.answer: Missing criteria reduce confidence. An unresolved identity produces an insufficient-data result, while unmatched artifacts produce a no-match result.

faq.question: Does it save or edit anything?
faq.answer: No. Results remain in the conversation, and the skill does not modify workspace files or artifacts.
